description: Rung-5 multi-step formula chains: dimensional word problems whose gold ADJ program needs TWO OR MORE chained let-bindings — an intermediate quantity is computed and then consumed by the next step (e.g. total_distance = leg1 + leg2; total_time = t1 + t2; answer = total_distance / total_time). This is the reasoning step beyond rung-4 dimensional arithmetic (which was a SINGLE operation): the model must DECOMPOSE the problem into ordered sub-results and let the engine carry dimensions through every link of the chain. The intermediate results (total_distance, total_time, …) are NEVER written as literals — the engine computes each and threads it forward — so the no-result-literals gate holds for the chain just as it did for one op. Five families: average speed over two legs (km/h), net displacement rate (km/h, via subtraction then division), combined density (g/ml), average power (j/s), and average flow rate (l/min). Every options set includes the signature multi-step TRAP — the average-of-the-two-ratios answer (which equals total/total only when the denominators are equal, so all items use UNEQUAL denominators to separate them) — plus a skip-a-step distractor (the numerator sum, undivided), a wrong-unit distractor (right magnitude, wrong dimension), and a single-leg ratio. A number-only or single-step reasoner falls for the average-of-ratios trap; only the engine, carrying the chained dimensional computation, lands the weighted total/total with the right unit. Reuses the compute_dimensioned extractor unchanged (it reads the final let binding 'answer' from the JSON derived section); no engine or harness change — pure new data exercising deeper let-chaining the engine already supports.

items.stem: A delivery van drives 120 kilometers in 2 hours, then 300 kilometers in 3 hours. What is its average speed over the whole trip?
items.program:
observe first_distance(quantity(120, km))
observe first_time(quantity(2, h))
observe second_distance(quantity(300, km))
observe second_time(quantity(3, h))
let total_distance = first_distance + second_distance
let total_time = first_time + second_time
let answer = total_distance / total_time
? answer

items.stem: A train passes the 20-kilometer marker and later the 140-kilometer marker, 2 hours apart. What is its average speed between the markers?
items.program:
observe start_marker(quantity(20, km))
observe finish_marker(quantity(140, km))
observe elapsed(quantity(2, h))
let net_distance = finish_marker - start_marker
let answer = net_distance / elapsed
? answer
